key_terms.meaning: Selecting an object and then changing its position, orientation or scale using a chosen technique plus a constraint.
The number of independent ways a body can move; a rigid body in space has 6 DOF (3 translation, 3 rotation).
A manipulation technique where the tracked hand position maps directly to a virtual hand that grabs objects it touches.
A virtual-hand variant where the hand grows and its reach extends nonlinearly once it passes a distance threshold.
Pointing with a ray from the hand or head and selecting or moving the object the ray hits; good for far objects.
Hand-centred Object Manipulation Extending Ray-casting: pick far object with a ray, then move it with the hand.
A rule that restricts manipulation to fewer DOF, such as move-on-plane, move-along-axis or snap-to-surface.
The interaction task of moving the user's viewpoint through the virtual world.
The cognitive task of deciding where to go and staying oriented, supported by maps, landmarks and signs.
A travel technique where the user points to a target and jumps there instantly, avoiding continuous motion sickness.
Interaction that changes the application itself (mode, tool, save, quit) rather than an object in the scene.
A menu drawn in the 3D space: list, Tring menu or pie menu, placed on the hand, on a wand or in the world.
Combining voice, gesture and menu input, where one channel disambiguates or confirms the other.
A tree of nodes, each holding a transform, geometry and state, that a toolkit traverses to draw the world.
The position, rotation and scale stored at a node, applied to everything below it in the tree.
Software that supplies an editor, scene model, asset pipeline, physics, lighting and a build path for VR and AR apps.
A saved, reusable object template that can be dropped into many scenes and updated in one place.
The Unity base class for a C# script attached to a game object, giving Start, Update and collision callbacks.
The Unity physics component that makes an object respond to forces, gravity and collisions.
The Unity callback that runs at the physics timestep, the correct place for force and physics code.
The delay between a user's real movement and the matching change in the display; motion-to-photon latency.
The mismatch between where the eyes focus and where they converge in a stereo headset, a cause of discomfort.
Nausea, dizziness and eyestrain caused by conflicting motion cues from the display and the body.
A 10-item questionnaire scored 0 to 100 giving a quick, comparable usability rating.
A six-subscale questionnaire measuring perceived mental, physical and temporal load on a task.
The user's sense of really being inside the virtual place rather than looking at a screen.

takeaways: 3D manipulation is selection plus a transform, and a good technique always trades reach against precision.
Constraints (axis, plane, snap) do most of the work of making 3D manipulation accurate on a phone-sized target.
Travel moves the viewpoint; wayfinding tells the user where to go, and confusing the two creates lost users.
Continuous travel suits small worlds, teleportation suits large worlds and comfort-sensitive users.
System control must be cheap to invoke and hard to trigger by accident, so voice and gesture need confirmation.
A scene graph exists so the renderer can cull, sort and draw a tree of nodes instead of tracking thousands of objects by hand.
Unity and Unreal differ more in workflow and scripting language than in the VR concepts they expose.
C# scripts plus a physics engine give interaction rules and stable collisions, not hand-authored animation.
Most VR sickness is predicted by latency, frame rate, acceleration and field-of-view; measure before shipping.
Usability in 3D is measured with task time, errors, SUS and NASA-TLX, and read together with think-aloud comments.
bank_note: Long answers here are judged on definition plus technique comparison plus a design decision for a stated scenario, so always name the task, the constraint and the comfort or usability consequence.

bank.q: Define 3D manipulation and break it into its subtasks. Explain how a constraint reduces the degrees of freedom of a manipulation.
outline: Definition: select an object, then change position, orientation or scale
Subtasks: selection, positioning, rotation, scaling
6 DOF for a rigid body; constraint restricts to a subset
Examples: move on plane, rotate about one axis, snap to surface
Why: tracked-hand accuracy is poor, constraints remove ambiguity and jitter
Effect on precision and on error recovery

bank.q: Compare the virtual hand, Go-Go and ray-casting techniques for object selection and manipulation. State one scene where each is the best choice.
outline: Virtual hand: direct, 1:1 mapping, natural, limited reach
Go-Go: nonlinear gain past threshold, extends reach, still proprioceptive
Ray-casting: works at any distance, poor for rotation and depth control
HOMER hybrid as an improvement
Best cases: nearby assembly, mid-range shelf, far control panel
Cost: tracking accuracy, arm fatigue, selection ambiguity

bank.q: Distinguish travel from wayfinding. Describe three travel techniques and three wayfinding aids with their trade-offs.
outline: Travel = viewpoint motion; wayfinding = deciding the route and staying oriented
Travel techniques: physical walking, steering, teleportation, ride-along
Steering: continuous, good for small worlds, causes sickness
Teleportation: comfortable, breaks presence continuity
Wayfinding aids: grid floor with compass, landmarks, embedded map, guided tours, breadcrumbs
Trade-offs: immersion versus comfort versus cognitive load

bank.q: Classify system control techniques in VR and explain each class with a short example.
outline: Definition: changes the application, not a scene object
Graphical: list menu, Tring menu, pie menu; hand or wand placement
Voice commands: hands-free, needs vocabulary, feedback and error handling
Gestural commands: quick, must avoid accidental matches with manipulation gestures
Tools: virtual tool belt
Multimodal: one channel selects, another confirms
Design points: cheap invocation, clear feedback, undo

bank.q: Explain what a scene graph is, what a node stores, and how a toolkit uses the tree when drawing a frame.
outline: Tree of nodes with parent-child transforms
Node contents: local transform, geometry, material and state, children
World transform = product of transforms up to the root
Traversal: cull by bounding volume, then draw; state inherited unless overridden
Efficiency: grouping, instancing, matrix reuse, sorting
Shared subtrees and dynamic nodes for tracked head and hands

bank.q: A user must place a small bolt into a hole 2 m away in a VR assembly trainer. Choose a manipulation technique and a set of constraints, and justify each choice.
outline: Far object, high precision, so start with ray-casting or HOMER
Constraint: move along the bolt axis, then snap-to-hole on approach
Reduction from 6 DOF to 1 DOF near the target
Haptic or audio confirmation on snap
Feedback: ghost preview of the target position
Comparison with plain virtual hand, which cannot reach 2 m
Comfort: avoid large arm extension for long sessions

bank.q: Design a locomotion and wayfinding scheme for a virtual walkthrough of a large heritage site. Give the travel technique, the aids and the comfort settings.
outline: World is large and continuous, so teleportation plus short-range steering
Point-and-teleport target marker with valid/invalid colouring
Wayfinding: overview map, landmark monuments, compass on the hand, guided tour mode
Floor grid or subtle vignette during motion
Speed limits, snap turning instead of smooth turning
Prevent teleporting through walls
Measure: task time to reach a named monument, number of lost events

bank.q: Write the structure of a C# script that lets a grabbed object follow the controller while collisions stay stable, and explain each part.
outline: MonoBehaviour class, serialised fields for speed, grabbed flag
OnTriggerEnter or XR interaction events to set grabbed state
Update reads controller pose; FixedUpdate moves the Rigidbody with MovePosition or force
Keep interpolation on, disable gravity while held
Constraints on the Rigidbody to lock unneeded axes
OnRelease restore velocity and gravity
Why FixedUpdate, not Update, for physics

bank.q: A headset runs at 90 frames per second. Compute the frame budget and explain how latency, physics timestep and script cost share it.
outline: Frame time = 1/90 s ≈ 11.1 ms
Budget split: tracking, simulation, rendering, compositor
Physics timestep independent of frame rate; interpolation
Heavy script work in Update misses the frame
Latency beyond about 20 ms is felt as lag
Fix: reduce draw calls, bake lighting, profile first

bank.q: Analyse the causes of simulator sickness in VR and evaluate four mitigations against them.
outline: Cause: sensory conflict between visual motion and vestibular signal
Cause: latency and low or unstable frame rate
Cause: vergence-accommodation conflict in stereo displays
Cause: wide field of view with high optic flow
Mitigations: teleportation or snap turn, motion vignette, high frame rate and low latency, fixed reference frame or cockpit
Evaluate each against comfort, presence and task cost
Session limits, breaks, user screening

bank.q: Design a usability evaluation for a 3D menu system and justify your choice of measures.
outline: Task-based test with defined tasks: open menu, change mode, undo
Metrics: task time, error rate, NASA-TLX for load, SUS for satisfaction
Think-aloud during learning, silent during timed trials
Expert review first to remove obvious faults
Fatigue measure over a longer session, arm and shoulder
Presence questionnaire if immersion matters
Compare against a baseline menu, counterbalance order, minimum sample size

bank.q: Evaluate whether voice, gesture or a graphical menu is the better system control channel for a hands-busy surgical training application. Justify with error, fatigue and feedback arguments.
outline: Hands busy sterilisable context favours voice
Voice problems: recognition error, vocabulary size, no private speech, delay
Gesture: no device needed but conflicts with manipulation gestures
Graphical menu: precise and visible but needs a hand or dwell
Multimodal: voice command with visual confirmation
Feedback required for every channel
Fatigue and error recovery, undo for all channels

bank.q: Trace the full path from a scene graph node to a lit stereo frame on the headset, and evaluate where latency and where bugs enter.
outline: Scene graph node, local and world transforms
Culling and sorting, draw call submission
Engine script updates from input before rendering
Eye transforms from head tracking, per-eye view and projection
Stereo rendering, distortion correction and compositing
Latency sources: tracking, simulation, render queue, display scan-out
Bugs: stale transforms, double transform application, update order
Measure with a profiling tool, not by eye

bank.q: You must build a VR training app in one semester with a small team. Choose Unity or Unreal and justify the choice across scene model, scripting, asset pipeline and build path.
outline: Engine components: editor, scene model, asset pipeline, lighting, physics, build
Unity: C#, component model, prefabs, wide XR plugin support, fast iteration
Unreal: Blueprints plus C++, stronger default rendering, heavier hardware
Team skill and hardware are the deciding factors
Asset import and texture and lightmap budget
Device SDK and store requirements
Prototype first, measure build time and frame rate before committing

glossary.def: The interaction task of selecting an object in 3D space and changing its position, orientation or size.
Choosing one object out of many as the target of the next action.
The count of independent motions a body can make; a free rigid body has six.
A manipulation technique that maps the tracked hand directly to a virtual hand that grasps objects.
A virtual-hand technique that stretches the reach nonlinearly once the hand passes a distance threshold.
Selection and manipulation by shooting a ray from the hand or head and acting on the first object hit.
A hybrid that selects a distant object with a ray and then manipulates it with the hand.
A restriction that cuts the allowed degrees of freedom, such as moving only along one axis.
The task of moving the user's viewpoint through the virtual world.
The cognitive task of choosing a route and keeping track of position and heading.
Travel by jumping the viewpoint to a pointed-at target instead of gliding there.
Interaction that changes the application or its mode rather than an object in the scene.
A radial menu where items sit around a circle and are chosen by direction rather than by distance.
Using two or more input channels, such as voice plus gesture, in one command.
A tree that stores the virtual world as nodes carrying transforms, geometry and state.
The position, rotation and scale of a node, inherited by its children.
Software providing an editor, scene model, rendering, physics and build path for interactive applications.
A reusable object template in Unity that can be instantiated and edited in one place.
The Unity base class for scripts that attach to game objects and receive update and collision callbacks.
A Unity component that subjects an object to the physics engine's forces, gravity and collisions.
The time from a real head movement to the matching change of light leaving the display.
Discomfort, nausea and eyestrain caused by conflicting visual and bodily motion cues.
The disagreement between the eye's focus distance and its convergence distance in a stereo headset.
The feeling of being located inside the virtual environment rather than observing it.
A ten-item questionnaire that yields a single 0 to 100 usability score.
A six-subscale questionnaire that scores perceived workload on a task.
